root_idea.summary: The root centers on likeness, correspondence, and conformity: one thing being like, aligned with, or brought into relation with another.
root_idea.development: From likeness and correspondence developed extensions involving binding a thing to its counterpart, resemblance in form or conduct, mixed coloration, and figurative confusion where things become indistinguishable or overlap.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized nominal citation form شَاكِلَةٌ.
Displayed as the nominal headword شَكْلٌ.

senses.definition: A person's characteristic manner, disposition, or course of action.
senses.usage_conditions: In عَلَى شَاكِلَتِهِ, it denotes the manner or disposition according to which a person acts, including the person's characteristic orientation, aim, or direction of conduct.

senses.definition: A like, counterpart, or corresponding kind.
senses.usage_conditions: In مِنْ شَكْلِهِ, it denotes something corresponding to another in form or manner; in the Quranic passage, it refers to punishment like the preceding punishment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To bind an animal's legs with a شِكَال or similar cord.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of horses, beasts, birds, and camels; the binding may join or restrain corresponding legs.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To mark or restrict writing with grammatical, vocalic, and other reading signs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A later or technical usage connected figuratively with removing ambiguity from writing; the source distinguishes it from merely dotting letters.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To plait two locks of hair and use them to bind the remaining locks.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Described of a woman arranging the hair at the front of the head.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To compress the lioness sexually.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare lexical usage reported on the authority of one early lexicographer.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To use amorous or coquettish gestures and behavior.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes amorous display combined with feigned coyness or opposition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To incline toward, rely upon, or find ease in something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction takes إِلَى with the object toward which one inclines or on which one relies.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To form, fashion, shape, sculpt, or picture something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative or transitive shaping use, synonymous with giving something a form or image.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Conformity, suitability, agreement, similarity, or homogeneity between things.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The related verb مُشَاكَلَ can describe things or persons as corresponding or resembling one another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become like or resemble something; to acquire a likeness or match.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The source presents this as the primary signification of the Form IV verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become dubious, confused, mixed up, or difficult to distinguish.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a thing, case, affair, or information becoming unclear to someone; إِشْكَالٌ can function as a noun for doubt or uncertainty.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be nearly cured while remaining in an uncertain intermediate state.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized usage said of a disease and compared with تَمَاثَلَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For date palms to reach the stage at which their dates are sweet and ripe or nearly ripe.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used specifically of the ripening state of palm dates.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For an eye to have the coloration called شُكْلَةٌ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The coloration is a reddish admixture in the white of the eye.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become formed, fashioned, shaped, or goodly in appearance and form.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive development into a particular shape or pleasing aspect.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For grapes to enter a partly ripened or darkening stage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes grapes becoming partly ripe, black, or beginning to ripen.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To deem a word, phrase, sentence, or statement dubious or confused.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A learned usage reported as current in the author's time.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A model, pattern, likeness, or manner corresponding to another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in expressions such as عَلَى شَكْلِهِ for being according to another's pattern or mode; the likeness sense is also represented by the Quranic form entry.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The shape, form, figure, or configuration of a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May refer to a perceptible or imagined form, including a body's outline or arrangement of boundaries.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A kind, sort, or variety.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of classes or varieties of animals, plants, food, and similar things.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Something suitable, fitting, or proper for a person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of what accords with someone's preferences, circumstances, or case.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A discordant, difficult, dubious, or confused affair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plural-derived usage referring to troublesome or unclear matters that cause anxiety or difficulty.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An ornament of pearls or silver resembling others of its kind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes ornaments worn by women as ear-drops or attached to the hair.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A species of plant diversified in color.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A botanical usage for a plant with yellow and red coloration.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The set of vowel marks and other signs indicating a word's pronunciation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical plural-like use of the verbal noun for the signs used to vocalize and disambiguate writing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Amorous, coquettish, or pleasing behavior.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used especially as an attribute of a woman and associated with coquettish charm and graceful dalliance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A white marking in an animal's flank.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Described of sheep or goats, with the rest of the coloration differing from the white flank.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The condition of an eye containing the coloration called شُكْلَةٌ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The referenced eye coloration involves a reddish admixture in the white.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An admixture of colors, especially redness mixed with whiteness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of the coloring of camels, sheep, goats, hyenas, and eyes; in an eye it denotes a reddish mark in the white, with variant descriptions recorded.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman who displays amorous or coquettish behavior in a pleasing manner.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexical designation for the woman rather than for the behavior itself.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A want, need, or requested matter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare nominal usage; the need is figuratively something that binds or constrains a person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dissimulation or conciliatory flattery.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare usage equated with مُدَاهَنَةٌ; the source leaves its precise grammatical category uncertain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cord, bond, or set of hobbles used to bind an animal's legs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of ropes joining or restraining the fore and hind legs of horses, camels, and other beasts; related saddle equipment has specialized applications.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A distinctive pattern of white markings on a horse's legs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The pattern involves contrasting marked and unmarked legs, with variant descriptions of which legs bear the markings.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Foam mixed with blood appearing around a bit's mouthpiece.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized equestrian usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A patch of white between an animal's cheek strap area and its ear.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized description of an animal's facial markings.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Uniform or made into one consistent arrangement.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression إِجْعَلِ الأَمْرَ شَوْكَلًا وَاحِدًا, ‘make the affair one uniform thing.’

other_classical_meanings.definition: The flank or side of a body.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In a horse, it may denote the skin or exterior region between the flank and the stifle area.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The hind legs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plural usage explained as arising from the legs being associated with or shackled by a شِكَال.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The point or aspect aimed at, especially the right point reached by an opinion or judgment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of the bodily-side sense in expressions about hitting the correct point.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The part between the ear and the temple.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized anatomical usage distinct from the flank sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Roads branching from a main road.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a road having multiple branches or diverging routes.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The two sides or margins of a road.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized plural construction describing the visible sides of a route.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The foot soldiers or a wing of an army.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Depending on usage, it denotes the infantry, the right wing, or the left wing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A side, region, quarter, or direction toward which one goes.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A general spatial or directional usage related to the notion of a side or branch.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A tree of the species called عَوْسَجٌ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A botanical designation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: More or most like something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A comparative adjective used with بِـ to indicate greater resemblance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having two colors intermixed, especially whiteness and redness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to blood, people, or other things; in water it can mean mixed with blood, and in an eye it describes a reddish mark in the white.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having blackness mixed with redness or dust-color.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied especially to camels, sheep, goats, and rams.

other_classical_meanings.definition: White in the flank or side marking.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a sheep or goat whose flank is white while the remainder is black; the feminine is شَكْلَاءُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The mountain species of lote tree.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A botanical term for a hard, thorny tree growing in high mountains and used for bows.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dubiousness, confusion, or entanglement.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun for a matter whose interpretation or identification is unclear.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A single tree of the species أَشْكَلُ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A botanical noun of unity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Entering among or becoming confused with things of its own kind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The participial sense emphasizes being mixed into a set of similar things.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A dubious, confused, or difficult matter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used substantively for a problem requiring clarification or resolution.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having white markings on the flanks.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized equestrian adjective.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Endowed with a pleasing aspect, appearance, or form.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjective describing good or attractive shaping.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A horse bound or shackled with a شِكَال.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive participial usage derived from the animal-binding sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A horse bearing the distinctive white-leg markings called شِكَالٌ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or specialized equestrian usage distinct from actual binding.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Writing supplied with grammatical, vocalic, and diacritical signs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical passive participle describing text whose pronunciation has been marked or restricted.

cautions: The two Quranic nominal forms express distinct constructions: شَاكِلَةٌ concerns a person's characteristic manner or disposition, while شَكْلٌ in 38:58 denotes a corresponding likeness or kind.
The writing-related senses of شَكَلَ and مَشْكُولٌ are technical or later usages and are kept among broader Classical Arabic meanings rather than assigned to the Quranic occurrences.
Several Lane citations are cross-references or rare specialized usages; these are retained only where the cited unit states lexical content, while pointer-only units remain audit metadata.
